Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

experience verb and noun

go through, find out by trying

also go through, undergo, an experience, know from experience, find out

classical

Cic. Fam. 13.9.3: illud tibi expertus prōmittō et spondeō
Cic. Planc. 22: dīcō expertus in nōbīs (Lewis & Short)

experior, experīrī, expertus sum

verb, fourth conjugation, deponent

try; in the perfect, know from experience

expertus, “from my own experience”; expertus sum, “I have been through it”. “An experience” has no single Latin noun: quod expertus sum, what I went through.

Examples

  • illud tibi expertus prōmittō et spondeō

    this I promise and guarantee you from my own experienceCic. Fam. 13.9.3

  • Sed et illud, quod vel Polliōnis vel tamquam Polliōnis accēpī, vērissimum experior

    and I find by experience that the saying I was given as Pollio’s, or as good as his, is very truePlin. Ep. 6.29.5

See also experience.
